title: The corner, i
logline: Wagner's Hardware on the corner is closing in the backgrounds. A month of dailies. Nobody says so. This is the first.

panels.composition: Main street, February. WOOD walking BARNABY, slowly, the dog on his own feet today. Behind them, the corner: WAGNER'S HARDWARE, a sign in the window the reader can just make out: EVERYTHING MUST.

image.prompt: a small-town main street in February, a man walking an old dog slowly, and behind them on the corner a hardware store with a hand-lettered sign in the window partly visible, muddy watercolor
image.notes: WAGNER'S HARDWARE — the vol 6/7 echo, in the background only. Sign: EVERYTHING MUST (GO cut off). Letter after.

panels.composition: Wood and the dog at the crosswalk. The strip is about the crosswalk. Behind: a man carrying a box out of Wagner's.

balloons.text: Nine years I've been waiting for this light to be better at its job.

image.prompt: a man and an old dog waiting at a small-town crosswalk, in the background a man carrying a cardboard box out of a hardware store

panels.composition: The dog, looking back at the store. Wood not.

image.prompt: close-up of an old dog looking back over its shoulder at a storefront while its owner looks straight ahead, no words

panels.composition: The light changes. They cross. Wagner's behind them, its door propped open with a paint can, the shelves inside half empty.
props: Wagner's door propped with a paint can

image.prompt: a man and a dog crossing a street, behind them a hardware store with its door propped open by a paint can and half-empty shelves visible inside, watercolor, no words

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; the Sundays the point now

notes: Wagner's closes in the backgrounds, Feb–Mar 2011. The strip never mentions it. The book takes two of twenty.
